text.p: Speculation intensified that Westinghouse Electric Corp will announce plans on Wednesday to split into two separate companies to boost shareholder value.
Investors have anticipated for several months that Westinghouse will create two separate stocks, one for a media company and one for its industrial operations.

Westinghouse spokeswoman Mimi Limbach declined to comment on a story in The Wall Street Journal Tuesday that said the Westinghouse board was meeting to approve the plan and the company would unveil it Wednesday.
Shares were up 5/8 in late-day trading on Tuesday to 20-5/8 amid heavy volume.

Analysts said Westinghouse will likely name the media company Westinghouse/CBS and locate corporate headquarters in New York. Its industrial operations will likely remain based in Pittsburgh, they said.

"But what they're going to call that company, is anybody's guess," said Nick Heymann at NatWest Heymann. He said Westinghouse will sell its headquarters building in downtown Pittsburgh and relocate employees to one of its industrial buildings located in various Pittsburgh suburbs.
Commercial real estate sources in Pittsburgh said recently that Westinghouse has been quietly seeking a buyer for the building. The company has repeatedly declined to comment.
"I understand they've been shopping that building around," said Rich Beynon at Beynon & Co, a commercial real estate firm.
Another real estate official who asked not to be identified said, "I can guarantee you they're going to sell that building. It's just a question of when."

Analysts said they couldn't confirm the board meeting or whether an announcement is forthcoming in the next day or two. "It's rumors we're hearing at this point," said Jonas Stiklorius at NatWest Securities.
Still, analysts said they would laud a separation plan because two companies would give investors the opportunity to value Westinghouse as a pure media play.
"Splitting the company into separate entities will get people focused on the part of the company they're most interested in," said Kent Newcomb at A.G. Edwards. "That clearly should be a positive.

Heyman said the media stock could trade above the company's current share value. "I think after the split we'll see new media coverage initiated and with a buy rating," he said. "I think the media stock (could trade up to 22)."

Heymann said the industrial stock will likely trade around 3 or 4. With the exception of Thermo King, a refrigerated transportation unit, Westinghouse's industrial operations have been a drag on earnings.

Conversely, the company's media performance has impressed Wall Street in recent months. Its radio operations posted a sales increase in the third quarter that outpaced the market, and CBS has consistently improved in the network ratings since it was bought by Westinghouse for $5.4 billion a year ago.
Westinghouse is expected to close its purchase of radio giant Infinity Broadcasting by year-end.
